en.name: Cheese curds
en.summary: Cheese curds are the young, un-pressed pieces of cheddar curd sold before they are milled into a wheel — mild, salty and squeaky when fresh. Refrigerated they keep about 2 weeks, and frozen about 4 months. The squeak is the first thing to go, long before anything else.
en.pantry: Curds are a fresh, high-moisture cheese and must not be kept at room temperature. Producers often sell them warm on the day they are made and people eat them that way, but that is a same-day proposition, not storage: follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour if the room is above 32 °C (90 °F), and refrigerate anything you are not eating now. A bag left in a warm car for an afternoon should be thrown out, not chilled and saved.
en.fridge: Keep curds at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a sealed bag or box, on an inside shelf rather than the door, and use them within about 2 weeks. Because they are fresh and unaged, they are moister and less acidic than a matured cheese, which is the profile that makes a cheese a Listeria monocytogenes risk — the organism grows slowly even at fridge temperature. Buy curds made from pasteurised milk, and if you are pregnant, elderly or immunocompromised, eat them cooked rather than raw.
en.freezer: Curds freeze reasonably well for about 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Bag them flat in portion sizes, press the air out and label the date; frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C, so the 4 months is about quality. They lose the squeak permanently — freezing rearranges the curd's protein structure — so freeze them for poutine, frying or melting rather than for snacking.
en.thawing: Thaw curds overnight in the fridge, never on the counter, and use them within a day or two. Do not refreeze them.
spoilage: Mould of any colour in the bag, including inside the fold at the top.
A sour, yeasty or fermented smell instead of a mild milky one.
A slimy or sticky surface, or liquid pooling in the bag.
tips: Buy the freshest bag you can find; the squeak is a freshness test in itself.
Portion them into small bags before freezing so you thaw only what you need.
Warm curds briefly in your hand, not the microwave, to bring the squeak partly back.
Keep the bag sealed — curds dry out and harden fast once air gets in.

faq.q: How long do cheese curds last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, sealed and on an inside shelf.
Yes, about 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F). They lose the squeak for good, so freeze them for cooking rather than snacking.

faq.q: Why have my cheese curds stopped squeaking?
faq.a: The squeak fades within days as the curd's protein structure relaxes, and refrigeration speeds that up. It is a sign of age, not of spoilage.

faq.q: Do cheese curds need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Yes. They are a fresh, high-moisture cheese. Eat them on the day if they are sold warm, otherwise keep them cold.

zh.name: 新鮮乳酪凝塊
zh.summary: 乳酪凝塊是切達乳酪在壓模成型之前的年輕凝乳塊，味道溫和帶鹹，新鮮時咬下去會「吱吱」作響。冷藏大約可以放 2 週，冷凍大約 4 個月。最先消失的是那個吱吱聲，遠早於其他任何變化。
zh.pantry: 凝塊是含水量高的新鮮乳酪，不能放室溫保存。產地常常在製作當天就把還溫熱的凝塊賣掉、大家也就這樣吃，但那是「當天吃完」，不是保存方式：請遵守 2 小時原則（室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時），沒有要馬上吃的就冰起來。在悶熱的車上放了一下午的那一袋，請丟掉，不要冰起來繼續留。
zh.fridge: 密封袋或密封盒裝好，放在 4 °C 以下的內側層架而不是門邊，約 2 週內吃完。因為它新鮮、未經熟成，含水量比熟成乳酪高、酸度也低，這正是乳酪會被列為李斯特菌風險的那種特性——這種菌在冷藏溫度下仍會緩慢生長。請選用巴氏殺菌乳製作的凝塊；孕婦、長者與免疫力低下者建議加熱後再吃，不要生食。
zh.freezer: 凝塊冷凍效果還不錯，在 −18 °C 下大約 4 個月。分成一次用量、壓平裝袋、擠出空氣並寫上日期；−18 °C 下食品的安全性是無限期的，4 個月講的是品質。吱吱聲會永久消失——冷凍會重組凝乳的蛋白質結構——所以請為了做肉汁乳酪薯條、油炸或融化而冷凍，不要為了直接當零嘴。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍，不要放室溫，解凍後一兩天內用完。不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 袋內出現任何顏色的霉，包括袋口摺起來的地方。
聞起來發酸、有酵母味或發酵味，而不是淡淡奶香。
表面黏滑，或袋底積出液體。
吃起來發苦或有氣泡感。
tips: 買你找得到最新鮮的那一袋；會不會吱吱叫本身就是新鮮度測試。
冷凍前先分小袋，之後只解凍需要的量。
想找回一點吱吱感，用手心稍微回溫就好，不要用微波爐。
袋口務必密封——一進空氣，凝塊很快就乾硬。

faq.q: 乳酪凝塊放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封後放 4 °C 以下的內層，大約 2 週。
可以，−18 °C 下約 4 個月。吱吱聲會永久消失，所以請為了入菜而冷凍。

faq.q: 為什麼我的乳酪凝塊不吱吱叫了？
faq.a: 那個聲音幾天內就會隨著凝乳蛋白質結構放鬆而消失，冷藏又會加快這個過程。這是變舊的跡象，不是壞掉。

faq.q: 乳酪凝塊一定要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 要。它是含水量高的新鮮乳酪。若買到還溫熱的現做品就當天吃完，其餘一律保持低溫。
